# NOTES: THE ANGEL OF THE REVOLUTION (George Griffith, 1894 ed., Tower Pub. Co.; Gutenberg #31324). Single book, no multiple BOOK headings.

## Front matter
- Frontispiece: "NATASHA" drawn by Edwin S. Hope. Illustrations by Fred. T. Jane. Fifth edition, London, Tower Publishing Co., 91 Minories, 1894. Dedicated to Cyril Arthur Pearson (suggested the story).
- Contents: I At the Eleventh Hour; II At War with Society; III A Friendly Chat; IV The House on Clapham Common; V The Inner Circle; VI New Friends; VII The Daughter of Natas; VIII Learning the Part; IX The Beginning of Sorrows; X The "Ariel"; XI First Blood; XII In the Master's Name; XIII For Life or Death; XIV The Psychological Moment; XV A Voyage of Discovery; XVI A Wooing in Mid-Air; XVII Aeria Felix; XVIII A Navy of the Future; XIX The Eve of Battle; XX Between Two Lives; XXI Just in Time; XXII Armed Neutrality; XXIII A Battle in the Night; XXIV The New Warfare; XXV The Heralds of Disaster; XXVI An Interlude; XXVII On the Track of Treason; XXVIII A Skirmish in the Clouds; XXIX An Embassy from the Sky; XXX At Close Quarters; XXXI A Russian Raid; XXXII The End of the Chase; XXXIII The Breaking of the Charm; XXXIV The Path of Conquest; XXXV From Chaos to Arcadie; XXXVI Love and Duty; XXXVII The Capture of a Continent; XXXVIII The Beginning of the End; XXXIX The Battle of Dover; XL Beleaguered London; XLI An Envoy of Deliverance; XLII The Eve of Armageddon; XLIII The Old Lion at Bay; XLIV The Turn of the Battle-Tide; XLV Armageddon; XLVI Victory; XLVII The Judgment of Natas; XLVIII The Ordering of Europe; XLIX The Story of the Master; Epilogue "And on Earth Peace!"

## Ch I–II (London, Sept 3, 1903)
- Richard Arnold, 26, Southwark tenement top floor, inventor of aerial navigation. Used two liquefied gases that explode spontaneously, admitted by clockwork escapement to cylinders. Inherited £2,000 from father; spent on ~5 years of experiments. Model air-ship flew in his room; he cried "Victory! It flies! I am master of the Powers of the Air at last!"
- Owes 12s rent; has ~2s and a half-crown. Sea-chest holds model. Reads Echo paragraph: Colonel Dornovitch (Imperial Police) stabbed at Kovno on Berlin–Petersburg express; "T" cut on forehead; Terrorists suspected. Passenger Lord Alanmere (formerly Viscount Tremayne, Trinity college friend) is Secretary to British Embassy at St Petersburg.
- Tsar offers £1,000,000 for air-ship. Arnold on Embankment near Cleopatra's Needle.
- Maurice Colston (Socialist, Savoy Mansions, servant Burrows) invites him. Shows knout scars from flogging for protesting a Jewess's death. Colston is Russian-tortured Terrorist. Arnold gets clothes.

## Ch III–IV
- Colston explains Ainsworth (CID inspector) killed by Terror for taking Russian bribe (£250 + £250); Birkett confessed falsely.
- Conditions: Arnold keeps gas formula; will not destroy defenceless people. Clapham Common house (Mr. Smith's). Ten sovereigns paid. Cab with telephone spies. Passwords in four languages: "Das Wort ist Freiheit", "Quien va?", "Por la libertad?", "Für Freiheit über alles!". Two French detectives buried under floor.

## Ch V–VI (Inner Circle, 14 masked members, 9 men 5 women)
- Paintings of Russian atrocities (woman flogged to triangle = Radna Michaelis, Colston's fiancée). Oath read; Arnold signs; paper burnt. President (Nicholas Roburoff) welcomes: "Master of the Air".
- Natasha: "daughter of Natas"; sapphire-blue eyes; white-haired Radna. Air-ship model described: aluminium hull 3 ft, helices, air-planes, four engines; named Ariel. Underground rifle range.
- Arnold ordered to Petersburg with Natasha and Princess Ornovski (Anna).

## Ch VII–VIII
- Natasha sings Hymn of Freedom. Colston: Radna's torturers: governor of prison (Brovno), prefect of police, spy, two soldiers. Colston killed three; others remain. Chief = Lord Alanmere, Natas's agent. Natasha's cover: Fedora Darrel, niece of Princess Ornovski (parents drowned on Albania).
- Colonel Martinov (secret police director) to be executed. Balloon offered to Tsar; Arnold to inspect. Lunch in Cheyne Walk.

## Ch IX (March 6, 1904, Inner Circle)
- Roburoff announces Natasha captured at Moscow (Bolshoi Dmitrietka, Alexei Kassatkin house); sentenced to Sakhalin; convict train via Nizhni Novgorod, Perm, Tiumen. Colston (Alexis Mazanoff) sent to rescue. Ariel to rescue at Tiumen before march on Friday 9th.
- Berlin "Terror" plans; secret Franco-Russian treaty; war within a month; Ivan Brassoff provokes Afghan frontier clash. Steamer Avondale to Rio cover, then island off West Africa (Cape Blanco–Cape Verde). Radna farewell kiss.

## Ch X–XI
- Drumcraig Island (Outer Hebrides, Chief's). Ariel: 70 ft; crew Andrew Smith (coxswain, English), Ivan Petrovitch (Russian), Franz Meyer (German), Jean Guichard (French). Flight 2,200 miles at 120 mph; Ariel rises over Scotland (Ben Lomond, Campsie Fells).
- Kronstadt shelled by Arnold and Colston (first shots); Arnold: "fire the first shot". Petersburg visible.

## Ch XII–XIII (Tiumen, Thursday)
- Ariel hidden in forest 5 miles east of Tiumen near Tobol road. Colston as fur merchant Stepan Bakuinin, Ivan as servant.
- Sub-commissioner Dmitri Soudeikin; forged passes; 2,000 roubles. Natas death sentence notice. Captain of convict train; Lieutenant guard; Captain Kharkov convoy. Governor of Tiumen.
- Colston kills sentry; Natasha and Princess Anna escape in disguise as peasant boys. Troika; Cossacks pursued; Ariel's searchlight; Ariel destroys Cossacks; note "The daughter of Natas sends greeting to the Governor of Tiumen".

## Ch XIV–XV
- Times, March 8, 1904 telegram: Kronstadt destroyed. Russian war-balloons (50 each). Council: Tsar's fleet of 50 balloons. Fight at Sir Ulang Pass.
- Louis Holt's manuscript (balloon found in Gulf of Guinea; "Aeria" = hidden valley). Arnold Natasha's love: "I love you."

## Ch XVI–XVII (Aeria, Africa)
- Arnold proposes; Natasha: "armed neutrality"; condition: no words of love till peace declared. Natasha heart-whole. Ariel crosses Red Sea, Abyssinia, Sahara; reaches Aeria mountain walls; leaps 6,000-ft ridge; Thomas Jackson waves; Louis Holt (grizzled, 55–70).

## Ch XVIII (May 20 onward)
- Avondale steamer meets Ariel off West Africa (~May 22). Roburoff and Radna aboard. Natas letter. Fleet of 12 ships; flagship Ithuriel (100 ft, five masts). Fleet in Aeria mid-June. Roburoff governs colony.

## Ch XIX (House of Lords speech, Tremayne vs Duke of Argyle; Loan Bill lost by 7; Balfour government; war declared by France; Italy defects; Queen Victoria abdicated.)

## Ch XX (Natas reveals Tremayne's double life; Natas physically crippled; Buddhist hordes prophecy; "Field of Armageddon" vision; Tremayne loves Lady Muriel Penarth of Marazion; deed of gift)

## Ch XXI–XXII (Aurania, Michael Roburoff; Lurline (yacht) sunk by French cruiser; Ithuriel intervenes; French cruiser disabled; Andromeda (British cruiser) Captain's comments)

## Ch XXIII–XXV (Aurania Atlantic; French/Italian squadron; Ithuriel destroys it; "Daily Telegraph" war summary; Aberdeen raid; Hiorring telegram re Baltic.)

## Ch XXVI–XXIX (Roburoff disgraced; Colston and Radna marry at Aeria; Lucifer stolen; Volnow arsenal; Tsar parley; Natas paralyses Volnow; Russian Colonel Alexandrovitch shot by Natas's paralysing gesture.)

## Ch XXX–XXXII (Copenhagen; Prabylov Admiral; Volnow killed; Lucifer recaptured in thunderstorm by grappling irons; deserters Peter Tamboff, Amos Vornjeh, Ivan Tscheszco, Paul Oreloff executed; Russian officers released Corunna.)

## Ch XXXIII–XXXV (Aberdeen falls; Berlin falls; Nile battle; Tremayne orders Michael Roburoff's death; Natasha learns Natas wanted her married to Michael; Arnold and Natasha kiss)

## Ch XXXVI–XXXVII (Michael executed by Natasha; Tremayne proclaims Federation in Washington; Ring punished exile Kodiak Island; Tremayne President.)

## Ch XXXVIII–XLII (Britain invaded; Battle of Dover; London besieged; King Edward VII accepts Federation; Mazanoff delegate; Harwich; Armageddon night; red signal.)

## Ch XLIII–XLVII (Tsar surrenders at Muswell Hill; Natasha sings; Natas judgment: mines of Kara for life; Tremayne Supreme Council.)

## Ch XLVIII–XLIX (European Constitution; Kaiser; Le Gallifet; Natas story of Israel di Murska and Sylvia Penarth; Natasha = Sylvia di Murska's daughter; Arnold marries Natasha; Tremayne marries Muriel; Christmas 1904.)

## Epilogue (1905: Constitution; Turkish war; Sultan Mohammed Reshad surrenders; Alexander Romanoff dies at Kara Dec 1, 1905; Arnold & Natasha baby at Aeria; "there is peace on earth at last".)
